Top candidates: White_Mold (white mycelium + sclerotia in stem), Charcoal_Rot (gray pith with microsclerotia), Brown_Stem_Rot (brown pith), Phytophthora (stem rot).

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a soybean stem split open lengthwise, held against a sky/bare-field background (late-season/post-harvest setting). The internal pith is grayish-white with brown discoloration along the center.

**Key comparisons:**
- **Brown_Stem_Rot 103 & 146**: Extremely similar — same split stem held in hand against sky/field background, same internal pith rot pattern. BSR 146 is nearly identical in composition (sky, field rows, roots visible at top, split stem).
- **Charcoal_Rot 116**: Shows gray pith with microsclerotia (tiny black dots) — the test image doesn't show these characteristic dots clearly.
- **White_Mold**: Shows exterior white mycelium and large black sclerotia — not matching.
- All other classes showed leaf spots, whole-plant wilting, seedling damping off, or pod/seed symptoms — not matching the split stem internal rot pattern.

The brown pith discoloration with light outer cortex, split open stem held in hand against a field background, matches Brown_Stem_Rot references 103 and 146 most closely.
